entries.name: Cavalry

licence.name: proprietary; free licence for individuals, enterprise terms through Canva (home page, 2026-11-02)

engines.name: Forge Dynamics
engines.does: Two-dimensional physics layer built on the Box2D library; bodies collide, fall and rest under gravity inside the scene.

engines.name: Particle Shape
engines.does: Particle system layer, marked a technical preview, that hosts emitters and modifier fields and outputs particles that can be shown as shapes.

engines.name: Node-based attribute graph
engines.does: Every layer attribute can be driven by another through connections, so a scene is a graph of nodes behind the layer list.

capabilities.does: Behaviours are nodes that animate or deform other layers. The docs list about 80 kinds, among them Noise, Oscillator, Spring, Wave, Random, Stagger, Bend Deformer, Lattice Deformer, Morph and Look At.
capabilities.inputs: layers or shapes plus behaviour attributes

capabilities.does: The Duplicator copies input shapes across a chosen distribution and can set position, rotation, scale, visibility, opacity, id and time offset for each copy.
A connection links one attribute to another so the first drives the second. An attribute takes one input and can feed many outputs; keyframes count as the input; only compatible data types connect.

Scripts in JavaScript run from a JavaScript Editor, from the Scripts menu, or inside JavaScript layers, utilities and deformers. Modules api, ctx, cavalry and def expose scene editing, per-layer context and deformer access.
capabilities.inputs: JavaScript code, layer ids, attribute paths
capabilities.outputs: created layers, changed attributes, computed values

capabilities.does: The Auto-Animate behaviour animates shapes from a few keys. Mode attributes set position, rotation, scale, opacity and visibility; timing attributes offset, randomise or reverse the order, including per line, word or character of text meshes.
capabilities.inputs: shapes or text meshes, Progress keys, mode attributes

capabilities.does: The Particle Shape hosts emitters (Distribution, JavaScript, Particle) and modifier fields such as Flow Field, Force, Goal, Turbulence and Vortex. Attributes cover lifespan, gravity, drag, mass, scale, rotation and colour over life.
capabilities.inputs: emitters, modifiers, input shape or image
capabilities.outputs: particles drawn as squares, circles or an input shape

capabilities.does: Forge Dynamics simulates rigid and soft bodies with Box2D. Body types are Dynamic, Still, Kinematic and Kinematic Hybrid; attributes include friction, bounce, density, collision groups and a ground mode; results can be cached.
capabilities.inputs: input shapes, body settings, fields, constraints

capabilities.does: Shape layers include Basic Shape, Editable Shape, Text Shape, SVG, Mesh Shape, Image to Shapes, Metaballs, Isolines, Trails, Corner Pin and Composition. A Group or Merge combines them.
capabilities.inputs: drawn paths, text, SVG files, images

capabilities.does: Exports a scene to Lottie JSON from the File menu or the Render Manager. Position, rotation, alpha, stroke trim and path animation export directly; filters, track mattes, dash patterns, skew and image sequences do not. Baking can be set per shape.
capabilities.inputs: a scene, per-shape Lottie baking mode
capabilities.outputs: a Lottie JSON file and an images folder

capabilities.does: The File menu has Render Current Frame to SVG, Export Selected, Export Lottie and Render Manager entries. Video and image sequence entries were not on the page read.
capabilities.inputs: the current frame or selected layers
capabilities.outputs: an SVG file or rendered output

scripting: JavaScript Shape, Utility and Deformer layers
outcomes: Lottie animations for apps and sites
motion graphics rendered through the Render Manager

entries.name: Rive

licence.name: editor: subscription with a free plan (free exports carry a splash screen); official runtimes: MIT

engines.name: Rive runtimes
engines.does: Open-source players that load a .riv file in web, React, React Native, Apple, Android, Flutter, Unity, Unreal and C++ apps and play its animations and state machines.

engines.name: Rive Renderer
engines.does: A drawing backend that the docs list separately from the runtimes; the docs also link a page on choosing a renderer.

engines.name: Luau scripting
engines.does: Scripts are written in Luau inside the editor and connect to data bindings, artboards and inputs.

capabilities.does: A state machine connects timeline animations as states with transitions in a graph. Each artboard has at least one; the example is a button with Idle, Hovered and Clicked states.
capabilities.outputs: interactive animation logic in the .riv file

capabilities.does: Listeners react to pointer enter, exit, move, down, up, drag and click, focus, blur, keyboard, gamepad, text input, semantic actions, view model changes and Rive events. Actions include View Model Change, Align Target, Focus Target, Report Event and Scripted Action.
capabilities.inputs: a target element or artboard, an event type

capabilities.does: Data is held as view model properties of twelve types: Number, String, Boolean, Color, Trigger, Enum, Image, Font, Blob, Artboard, View Model and List. Image, font and artboard properties let each instance show a different asset.
capabilities.outputs: scene properties updated from app data

capabilities.does: The Bone tool (key B) places chained bones; the first is the root with X and Y. Bones bind to vector path vertices or to image meshes, with per-vertex weights, Auto-Weights (Blend and Influence), Smooth and weight locking.
Constraints control an object's properties through a target object. The overview names six types: IK, Distance, Transform, Translation, Scale and Rotation; it gives no per-type detail.
capabilities.inputs: a constrained object and a target

capabilities.does: Easing types are Linear (default), Cubic, Cubic Value, Hold and Elastic (with Amplitude and Period). Cubic is set in the Interpolation panel with draggable handles; a four-number field takes values between 0 and 1.
A Graph Editor button on the timeline swaps the timeline for a curve view of the selected objects, with Bezier handles on Cubic Value keys that can overshoot the end value.
Scripts are written in Luau in the same editor as the design. They can be made by hand or with the AI Agent, are debugged in a Debug panel, and use protocols that set the script type.
Animate mode exports H.264, GIF, PNG Sequence, SVG Sequence and WebM; design mode exports PNG and SVG. Settings are Animation, Format, FPS, Duration, Bit rate and Size. A paid plan is required.
capabilities.inputs: an animation or artboard, export settings

capabilities.does: The .riv file loads in official MIT-licensed runtimes: Web (JS), React, React Native, Apple, Android, Flutter, Unity, Unreal, C++ and C#. Community runtimes exist for QtQuick, UWP and RiveCMP.
capabilities.outputs: playback inside an app, game or website

outcomes: interactive animations for apps, games and sites
icons, buttons and onboarding animations with state machines
exported video, GIF and image sequences

Expression interpolation: linear(), ease(), easeIn() and easeOut(), each in a form with input range tMin, tMax and two values and a short form where t runs between two values. Ease has zero velocity at both ends; easeIn and easeOut ease one side only.
Random helpers: random(), gaussRandom() for bell-shaped values, noise() that returns smooth values from minus one to one, and seedRandom(offset, timeless) to fix the sequence.

Property methods wiggle() and temporalWiggle() add random motion, smooth() averages a property over time, valueAtTime() reads the value at another time, and velocity and speed give its rate of change.

KeyframeEase holds a speed value and an influence value from 0.1 to 100, the numbers shown in the keyframe velocity dialog; ease arrays are given to setTemporalEaseAtKey.

AV layer attribute blendingMode sets how a layer combines with those beneath; preserveTransparency keeps the underlying alpha.
AV layer attribute trackMatteType selects a matte from the layer above; adjustmentLayer makes a layer apply its effects to the layers below.
timeRemapEnabled turns on time remapping for a layer, and canSetTimeRemapEnabled tells a script whether it is allowed.
precompose() moves chosen layers into a new composition, optionally moving all their attributes with them.
Composition attributes motionBlur and shutterAngle control blur from moving layers.
The AV layer attribute motionBlur turns motion blur on for one layer.
The AV layer attribute threeDLayer switches a layer into 3D space.
LayerCollection addCamera(name, centerPoint) and addLight(name, centerPoint) create camera and light layers in a composition.
CompItem attributes renderer and draft3d choose the composition renderer and a draft 3D mode.

Advanced 3D is a GPU-based composition renderer beside Classic 3D and Cinema 4D. It renders imported GLTF, GLB, OBJ and FBX models, HDRI environment lighting with shadows, and 3D text, shape and solid layers using Adobe Standard Material.
CompItem exposes layers, renderer, bgColor, resolutionFactor, shutterAngle, motionBlur, draft3d and workAreaStart; duplicate() copies a composition and openInViewer() shows it.

A child layer's transform values become relative to its parent, so moving the parent moves the child equally. Position, Scale, Rotation and Orientation follow; Opacity does not. A layer has one parent, a parent can have many children, and null layers can serve as parents.

Text layers can be animated through their Transform properties, animation presets, changes to the source text over time, or text animators with selectors that affect chosen characters. Motion blur smooths animated text.

The Content-Aware Fill panel replaces a masked area by synthesising pixels from other frames. Fill Method offers Object (moving things), Surface (flat static areas) and Edge Blend (fast, for plain surfaces); Alpha Expansion enlarges the filled region.

capabilities.does: Behaviors apply animation or simulation to layers, cameras and lights without keyframes, and some drive single parameters. They can be combined. Drag one from the Library onto a layer or use the toolbar pop-up, then adjust it in the Behaviors Inspector or HUD.

Interpolation sets the curve shape between keyframes: Constant holds then jumps, Linear is uniform, Bezier uses tangent handles, Continuous computes tangents itself, Exponential and Logarithmic bend the curve, and Ease In, Ease Out and Ease Both soften entry or exit.

The Keyframe Editor lists keyframeable parameters beside a graph of their curves. A Show Curve Set menu filters the list, and three tools edit curves: Edit Keyframes, Sketch Keyframes (draw a curve that generates keyframes) and Transform Keyframes (move a selected group).

A particle system has an emitter, an effect on a layer that multiplies it, and cells, the image layers duplicated and animated. Emitter parameters set shape and direction; cell parameters shape each particle. Cells can be images, shapes, text or movies.

A replicator copies a source layer into a pattern such as a spiral, circle or box; cell parameters set angle, colour and scale per copy. Patterns are static unless keyframed or driven by behaviors. Sequence Replicator staggers position, scale and opacity.

A rig maps preset values of many parameters to one control, called a widget: slider, pop-up menu or checkbox. Widgets can drive almost any parameter, even other widgets. Rigs can be published in Final Cut Pro templates to give editors a small control set.

2D layers can be rotated or placed in 3D space and intersect each other. Converting a project to 3D adds cameras with behaviors (dolly, pan, zoom), lights, environment lighting, shadows that objects cast and receive, and reflections.

Text can be animated with behaviors, keyframes or both. Text Sequence behaviors are presets such as Blur In or Squish. Text Animation behaviors cover scrolls and crawls, text tracking, type-on and custom character-by-character sequencing of colour, outline, opacity and scale.

Effects, titles, transitions and generators made in Motion are saved as Final Cut Pro templates and appear in the matching Final Cut browser. The author chooses which parameters to publish, giving the editor full, partial or no control. Projects can convert to and from templates.

Six tracking behaviors record a clip's movement, rotation or scale change and apply it to a target such as an image, particle emitter, filter, mask or text. They can also pass one animated object's motion to another or track a filter or object position.

MorphSVG morphs one SVG path into another shape. Options choose linear or rotational type, rotation origin, start-point offset shapeIndex, segment matching map, smoothing, curveMode and output precision; it can also draw to canvas.

Observer detects wheel, touch, pointer and scroll input through one callback set: onUp, onDown, onLeft, onRight, onChange, onPress, onDrag, onHover, onClick, with tolerance, axis locking and debounce.

engines.does: A motion component for React with animation, gesture, layout and presence props. Installed as the motion package and imported from motion/react.

engines.name: Motion for JavaScript
engines.does: Framework-free functions such as animate and scroll, working on HTML, SVG and other values.

capabilities.outputs: controls: play, pause, stop, cancel, complete, time, speed, then

animate() also takes an array of animate definitions that play in order by default. The at option places a segment by time, label, the symbol < or a relative offset; callbacks can sit in the array.

capabilities.inputs: animation or callback, container, axis, target, offset

engines.name: Smooth scroll core
engines.does: Takes over wheel and touch scroll and interpolates the scroll position each frame, by linear interpolation (lerp) or by duration and easing.

capabilities.does: Smooths scrolling with lerp (default 0.1) or duration (1.2 s) and easing. Options cover orientation, gesture orientation, wheel and touch multipliers, infinite scroll, nested scrolling, reduced-motion respect, anchors and automatic resize.

entries.name: FFmpeg

licence.name: LGPL-2.1-or-later by default; GPL-2.0-or-later when optional GPL parts such as libx264 are built in

engines.name: Transcoding pipeline
engines.does: Input files go through demuxer, decoder, optional filtergraph, encoder and muxer. Stream copy skips decoding and encoding.

engines.name: Filtergraph engine
engines.does: Chains of filters joined by commas, parallel chains joined by semicolons, linked through labels in square brackets. Used for audio, video, sources and sinks.

engines.name: Codec layer
engines.does: Documented software encoders include libx264, libx265, libvpx, libaom-av1, libsvtav1, librav1e, prores_ks, aac, libopus and flac, plus hardware encoders for NVENC, QSV and VAAPI.

engines.name: Container layer
engines.does: Muxers and demuxers for mov/mp4, Matroska/WebM, HLS, DASH, segment, tee, image2, GIF, MPEG-TS and FLV, each with private options.

engines.name: Scaler
engines.does: The scale filter resizes video with libswscale.

capabilities.does: Simple filtergraphs (-vf, -af) apply to one stream. Complex ones (-filter_complex, same as -lavfi) take several inputs and outputs, wired by link labels. Commas chain filters; semicolons separate chains.
Filters that support timeline editing accept an enable option holding an expression with t (seconds), n (frame number), pos, w and h, so a filter acts only during a time span.

-map picks streams from inputs or filter outputs; -c sets a codec per stream and -c copy passes packets through unchanged; -vn, -an and -sn drop video, audio or subtitles; -metadata and -disposition edit tags and flags; -map_chapters copies chapters.
-ss seeks, -t limits duration, -to sets an end time and -itsoffset shifts an input. Frame limits use -frames; -r, -s and -aspect set frame rate, size and display aspect ratio.
The concat filter joins audio and video segments end to end, with options n (segments), v and a (stream counts per segment) and unsafe.

The scale filter resizes with width and height expressions, force_original_aspect_ratio, force_divisible_by, reset_sar, scaling flags, colour range options and an eval option. setdar and setsar set aspect ratios.

crop (w, h, x, y, keep_aspect, exact), pad (width, height, x, y, color, aspect), rotate (angle in radians, output size, fillcolor), transpose (dir) and hflip change frame size and orientation; perspective takes four corner points.
overlay places one video over another at x and y expressions, with eval, shortest, format, repeatlast, alpha handling and eof_action options. Both inputs come from a filter graph.
capabilities.inputs: base video, overlay video, position expressions

capabilities.does: blend combines two inputs per component with a mode, opacity or expression (c0_mode to all_mode and matching opacity and expr options). tblend blends successive frames of one input with the same modes.
capabilities.inputs: two video inputs, mode per component

capabilities.does: xfade cross-fades between two inputs. Options: transition (effect type), duration, offset (start time) and expr (custom transition expression). fade applies fade-in or fade-out with type, start_frame, nb_frames, start_time, duration, alpha and color.
capabilities.inputs: two clips, transition name, duration, offset

capabilities.does: drawtext renders text or a text file with libfreetype. Options include text, textfile, fontfile, fontsize, fontcolor, box, boxcolor, borderw, x, y and expansion; drawbox draws coloured boxes.

The subtitles filter draws subtitle files onto video through libass. Options: filename, original_size, fontsdir, alpha, charenc, stream_index, force_style, wrap_unicode and shaping. An ass filter also exists for ASS files.
zoompan animates zoom and pan over a still or video using expressions for zoom z, x and y; options d (duration in frames), s (output size) and fps.
capabilities.inputs: zoom, x, y expressions, duration in frames

capabilities.does: setpts rewrites frame timestamps from an expression (speed up, slow down, offset) and asetpts does so for audio; atempo changes audio tempo. select and aselect pass only frames matching an expression; framestep keeps one frame in N.
fps converts to a constant frame rate by dropping or duplicating frames (options fps, start_time, round, eof_action).
minterpolate converts frame rate by motion-compensated interpolation. Options include fps, mi_mode, mc_mode, me_mode, me, mb_size, search_param, vsbmc, scd and scd_threshold.
capabilities.inputs: video, target fps, motion estimation options

capabilities.does: lut3d applies a 3D LUT file (options file, interp). lut, lutrgb and lutyuv apply per-component lookup expressions (c0 to c3, r, g, b, a, y, u, v) for custom tone maps.

colorchannelmixer remixes channels with rr to aa weights; colorbalance adjusts shadows, midtones and highlights per channel (rs to bh); colorlevels sets input and output levels; colorcorrect adjusts white balance; colortemperature simulates temperature shifts.
curves maps key points per channel (master, red, green, blue, all), loads Photoshop curve files with psfile, offers presets, interp choice and a plot output.
capabilities.inputs: preset, key points or curve file

capabilities.does: tonemap maps colours between dynamic ranges with options tonemap, param, desat and peak. zscale converts size, range, primaries, transfer and matrix using z.lib, including input-side variants.

chromakey makes a chosen colour transparent in YUV space (color, similarity, blend, yuv); colorkey does so in RGB (color, similarity, blend). chromahold removes colour from everything except one target colour.
lumakey turns pixels transparent by brightness, with threshold, tolerance and softness options.

vidstabdetect analyses camera motion in a first pass (result, shakiness, accuracy, stepsize, mincontrast, tripod) and vidstabtransform applies smoothed corrections in a second pass (smoothing, optalgo, maxshift, maxangle, crop, zoom, interpol).
hqdn3d denoises in space and time; gblur (sigma, steps), boxblur and unsharp blur or sharpen; noise adds grain per component with seed, strength and flags options.
capabilities.outputs: denoised, blurred, sharpened or grainy video

capabilities.does: geq evaluates one expression per pixel for each plane or colour; lenscorrection fixes radial distortion (cx, cy, k1, k2); vignette adds or removes vignetting (angle, x0, y0, mode, eval).

palettegen builds an optimised palette from video (max_colors, reserve_transparent, stats_mode). paletteuse applies it with dither, bayer_scale, diff_mode and alpha_threshold, for GIF output with controlled colours.

amix mixes several audio inputs into one; amerge combines streams into a multi-channel stream; join and channelsplit merge or split channel sets; pan remaps channels with an output layout and channel definitions; volume sets gain.

Audio effects: afade (type, curve, duration), acompressor, agate, alimiter, equalizer, highpass, aecho, adelay; aresample and aformat set rate and format; atrim keeps one section and areverse reverses audio.

loudnorm normalises to the EBU R128 standard with targets I, LRA and TP, plus offset, linear, dual_mono and print_format options. silenceremove trims silence (start_periods, stop_periods, thresholds, detection, window).

ebur128 analyses EBU R128 loudness and can draw a loudness graph (options video, size, meter, target, gauge, peak, framelog). astats reports time-domain statistics; aphasemeter measures stereo phase; showwaves, showspectrum, avectorscope and ahistogram draw audio as video.

libx264 and libx265 are configured with x264opts, x264-params and x265-params key=value lists; libx264 also has a53cc and udu_sei, libx265 has x265-stats for two-pass. General codec options include b, g, bf, qmin, qmax, maxrate, bufsize, profile and level.
libvpx covers VP8 and VP9 encoding. Listed options include lossless (VP9), tile-columns, aq-mode, row-mt, enable-tpl, ts-parameters for temporal layers and ref-frame-config.

libaom-av1 (cpu-used, aq-mode, tune, crf, tiles, aom-params), libsvtav1 (preset, crf, qp, hielevel, tile_rows, tile_columns, svtav1-params) and librav1e (speed, qp, tiles, rav1e-params) are the documented AV1 encoders.
The prores_ks encoder has options profile, quant_mat, bits_per_mb, mbs_per_slice, vendor and alpha_bits. The prores_aw encoder lists no private options.

NVENC has options preset, tune, rc, multipass, cq, rc-lookahead, spatial-aq, temporal-aq, gpu and split_encode_mode; QSV has async_depth, preset, forced_idr, low_power and qsv_params; VAAPI has low_power, idr_interval, b_depth, async_depth, max_frame_size and rc_mode.

mov/mp4 muxer options include movflags (faststart, frag_keyframe, default_base_moof), brand and use_editlist; Matroska has cues and cluster options; MPEG-TS has PID, service and PCR options; FLV has flvflags; the tee muxer writes one encode to several outputs.

The hls muxer writes playlists and segments (hls_time, hls_list_size, hls_segment_type mpegts or fmp4, encryption keys, var_stream_map for variants, master playlist). The dash muxer has seg_duration, use_template, use_timeline and low-latency options; the segment muxer splits by time or frame.
capabilities.outputs: HLS or DASH segments and playlists

capabilities.does: The image2 demuxer reads numbered images (pattern_type none, sequence or glob; framerate; start_number) and the image2 muxer writes them (frame_pts, update, strftime, atomic_writing).
capabilities.outputs: video from images, or images from video

capabilities.does: Command-line switches for unattended runs: -y overwrite, -n refuse overwrite, -progress for machine-readable progress, plus -f to force a format, so scripts can drive many conversions.
Source filters generate video without input: color (solid fill), testsrc and testsrc2 test patterns, gradients (linear, radial, circular, spiral, square types, up to eight colours c0 to c7).
eq sets brightness, contrast, saturation and gamma (with per-channel gamma and an eval option). hue changes hue and saturation. negate inverts components, optionally including alpha.
The concat demuxer reads a list file with file, duration, inpoint and outpoint entries and options safe and stream, joining files without a filter.
-hwaccel selects hardware-accelerated decoding and -hwaccel_device selects the device it runs on.

entries.name: MLT Multimedia Framework

licence.name: LGPL-2.1 (per the GitHub API; the README calls MLT an LGPL multimedia framework for video editing)

engines.name: Service graph
engines.does: Producers supply frames, filters change them, transitions blend two inputs and consumers output them. Playlist, multitrack, tractor, field and link are further building blocks.

engines.name: Property system
engines.does: Every service and frame holds a lookup table of named properties (strings, numbers, data pointers) that carries settings.

capabilities.outputs: composite timeline as a single producer

capabilities.does: 2D nodes are grouped into nine categories: Image, Draw, Time, Channel, Color, Filter, Keyer, Merge and Transform.
The plug-in nodes section holds FurnaceCore (included in NukeX and Studio), CaraVR, Ocula and Katana nodes; CaraVR and Ocula need their own licences and Katana nodes come from Katana 4.5 or later.
Toolsets nodes hold custom tools built inside Nuke, which users can create or modify. Utility nodes also cover views, metadata and script or viewer management.
Reusable tools are described as Gizmos, Toolsets and Presets.
VariableSwitch chooses between variables and scopes, which controls which of them are active in the script.

Merge combines inputs with a chosen operation. Controls: A channels, B channels, output, also merge, mask, inject, invert, fringe, mix, set bbox to, metadata from, range from and a video colourspace choice.
capabilities.inputs: A and B images, optional mask

capabilities.does: Merge operations: atop, average, color-burn, color-dodge, conjoint-over, copy, difference, disjoint-over, divide, exclusion, from, geometric, hard-light, hypot, in, mask, matte, max, min, minus, multiply, out, over, overlay, plus, screen, soft-light, stencil, under, xor.
Merge group also offers Premult, Unpremult, Matte, In, Out, KeyMix, Blend, Dissolve, TimeDissolve, Switch, CopyBBox, CopyRectangle, ContactSheet and ZMerge for depth-based merging.

Keylight controls: View, Unpremultiply Result, Screen Color, Screen Gain, Screen Balance, Alpha Bias, Despill Bias, Screen PreBlur; Screen Matte with Clip Black, Clip White, Clip Rollback, Dilate, Softness, Despot; Tuning; Inside Mask and Crops.
Keyer group: ChromaKeyer (GPU capable), Difference, HueKeyer, IBKColor with IBKGizmo, Keyer (a bundle of simple keyers), Keylight, Primatte and Ultimatte.

Cryptomatte reads ID mattes that renderers such as V-Ray and RenderMan write, and lets the artist pick individual mattes from the sequence, for example as a grading mask. The manifest comes from image metadata or a sidecar JSON, and matte boundaries can be previewed.

Roto draws and edits Bezier and B-spline shapes. Tabs: Roto (output, premultiply, clip to, replace, mask, opacity, feather, falloff, feather type), Transform, Motion Blur, Shape, Clone, Lifetime and Tracking with CornerPin export.
RotoPaint adds paint tools such as Clone, Blur and Dodge to Roto.

Tracker has a tracks table (track_x, track_y, offset, T, R, S, error); transform modes none, stabilize, stabilize 1pt, match-move, match-move 1pt, remove jitter, add jitter; auto-tracking with predict and warp type; keyframe tracking; CornerPin2D export.
Stabilize removes unwanted camera movement, rotation and scaling from a clip.

CameraTracker settings: number of features, detection threshold, feature separation, minimum length, track threshold, camera motion, lens distortion, focal length, film back, keyframe spacing, refine solve and stereo options. An export menu with Create and Link output controls includes a point cloud option.

SmartVector calculates SmartVectors for the SmartVector tool set, VectorToMotion converts them into motion, forward and backward channels, and VectorGenerator creates images holding motion vector fields.
VectorCornerPin uses SmartVectors to propagate an image over several frames and VectorDistort uses them to propagate paint.
Transform translates, rotates, scales and skews; TransformMasked adds a mask; Card3D, Reformat, Crop, Position, Mirror, Tile and AdjustBBox handle placement, format and bounding box.
CornerPin2D replaces a four-cornered feature with another image sequence.
SplineWarp warps with shapes or pins; GridWarp maps one Bezier grid onto another; GridWarpTracker drives grids from tracking data.
STMap moves pixels by absolute positions and IDistort warps by the UV channels.
LensDistortion estimates lens distortion; SphericalTransform converts between projections.

Kronos retimes with motion vectors. Timing is by frame or by input and output speed; method Frame, Blend or Motion; motion estimation Local or Regularized; vector detail, shutter time, shutter samples, matte, resampling Bilinear, Lanczos4 or Lanczos6.
Time nodes: Retime, TimeWarp, TimeOffset, TimeClip, FrameHold, FrameRange, FrameBlend, TimeBlur, TimeEcho, AppendClip, TemporalMedian, plus pulldown add and remove.
Grade controls: blackpoint, whitepoint, lift, gain, multiply, offset, gamma, black clamp, white clamp, mask and mix.
Colour group quick adjusters: ColorCorrect for contrast, gamma, gain and offset, Exposure, Gamma, Add and Multiply, Invert, Clamp and Posterize.
OCIOColorSpace converts between colour spaces with channels, input, output, swap, mask, unpremult and mix controls plus a context tab of four key and value pairs.

Other OCIO nodes: OCIODisplay applies a conversion for display, OCIOLookTransform applies a creative look from the config, OCIOCDLTransform applies an ASC CDL grade, OCIOFileTransform applies a LUT file, OCIOLogConvert converts compositing_log and scene_linear.
The product page lists OpenColorIO and ACES support for colour management.
ColorLookup adjusts through curves or LUTs, OCIOFileTransform applies a LUT file, Vectorfield applies pre-calculated LUT files, and Log2Lin and PLogLin convert log to linear.
GenerateLUT creates LUTs from colour management nodes.
MatchGrade calculates a grade to match two inputs and ColorTransfer matches one clip colours to another.
HueCorrect adjusts saturation within hue ranges; HSVTool adjusts hue, saturation and value; Saturation, HueShift, Posterize and Toe offer simple controls.
SoftClip compresses HDR imagery into zero to one; RollOffContrast applies a contrast curve across channels; ClipTest shows zebra on out-of-range pixels.
Histogram graphs pixel counts per brightness level and Sampler converts a horizontal scanline into a lookup curve.
CurveTool analyses the input to draw animation curves.
Filter group: Blur, Bilateral, Defocus, DirBlur, EdgeBlur, Median, Sharpen, Soften, Convolve, Erode variants, Emboss and EdgeDetect.
ZDefocus blurs by a depth channel. Controls include math, depth channel, focus plane, size at infinity, maximum, filter type (disc, bladed, image), aspect ratio and depth of field.

Denoise has a noise analysis (analysis region, frame, lock, import and export), film or digital source, constant or modulated model, denoise amount, roll off, smoothness, preserve edges, temporal processing with a Motion input and frequency tuning.

Inpaint fills an area marked in the source alpha or the Matte input using surrounding pixels. Stretch controls bias the fill direction, and Detail controls clone high-frequency texture from elsewhere or from the Detail input. GPU acceleration is supported.
MotionBlur adds blur to a sequence, VectorBlur smears pixels along vectors, and MotionBlur2D and MotionBlur3D convert transforms to UV vectors.

Flare simulates lens flares from reflections between lenses, Glint makes star-shaped rays around bright points, Sparkles creates rays in the viewer, and LightWrap reflects merged background light around foreground edges.
Grain adds synthetic grain, ScannedGrain applies scans of real film grain, Dither adds noise to hide quantisation, and DustBust removes dirt and scratches from scans.
Shuffle reorders up to eight channels, Copy and ShuffleCopy swap channels between inputs, ChannelMerge, AddChannels and Remove manage channel sets.
Draw group generators: Ramp, Radial, Noise (Perlin based), Grid, Rectangle and Text for overlays on images.
Image group generators: CheckerBoard, ColorBars (SMPTE pattern), ColorWheel and Constant (one colour in every pixel).

Classic 3D: 69 nodes for geometry (Card, Cube, Cylinder, Sphere, ReadGeo), cameras, lights (Light, Direct, Point, Spot, Environment), materials (BasicMaterial, Phong, Diffuse, Specular, Emission), geometry edits and scene assembly. The page says USD-based nodes supersede them.
ScanlineRender projection modes perspective, orthographic, uv, spherical and rendercamera; antialiasing none to high; samples, shutter, motion vector modes, overscan, filter and Z-blend mode.
Project3D projects an image through a camera onto an object; UVProject sets UV coordinates; Relight relights 2D images with 3D lights.
PointCloudGenerator builds a dense cloud from CameraTracker data, PoissonMesh makes a mesh from it, and DepthGenerator, DepthToPoints and DepthToPosition build geometry from depth.
The new 3D system builds on USD stage, prims and layers, with user guide topics for importing, paths and masks, cameras, projections, materials and shaders, lights, rendering and export.
Release 17.1 adds Hydra 2.0 support and the GeoRender node with GeoRenderSetting, GeoRenderProduct and GeoRenderVariable, plus ScanlineRender2 cutouts.
Release 17.1 adds Gaussian splat relighting, a GeoSequencer node and GeoExport support for splats.

Fourteen deep nodes: DeepRead, DeepWrite, DeepMerge (with holdouts), DeepRecolor, DeepColorCorrect, DeepCrop, DeepExpression, DeepFromFrames, DeepFromImage, DeepReformat, DeepSample, DeepToImage, DeepToPoints and DeepTransform.

NukeX and Studio particle nodes: ParticleEmitter, ParticleSpawn, forces (gravity, wind, turbulence, drag, vortex, point and directional force), ParticleBounce off 3D shapes, ParticleExpression, ParticleBlinkScript, ParticleCache and ParticleToGeo.
Write renders to disk. Write controls: channels, file, proxy, output transform, premultiplied, raw data, views, file type, create directories, render order and frame range.
MOV writer codecs: Animation, ProRes variants, Avid DNxHD and DNxHR, H.264, Motion JPEG A and B, MPEG-4, NotchLC, Photo-JPEG, PNG and Uncompressed; MXF writes DNxHD and DNxHR in OP-1A and OP-Atom.
Read loads images from disk and converts them to 32-bit linear RGB; UDIM Import brings in texture patches that follow UDIM numbering.
Nuke Studio reads and writes OTIO, EDL, AAF (read) and XML timelines.
Nuke Studio provides a customisable multi-track editorial timeline.
Release 17.1 review tools: Version Compare, sequence-aware Contact Sheet, Monitor Out interactive mode, Annotations shapes tool and burn-in of custom metadata with expressions.
Nuke and Hiero Python scripting engine for interface and higher-level node manipulation, with developer and reference guides.
Nuke Developer Kit is a C++ API for building operators; a USD C++ API reference covers the USD-based system.
The Blink API and BlinkScript write image-processing kernels that can target CPU or GPU.
CatFileCreator makes .cat files from TorchScript models for use in the Inference node.

entries.name: DaVinci Resolve (and Resolve Studio)

licence.name: Free edition plus paid Studio edition (one-off price USD 236 on the page read); Studio adds AI, noise reduction, HDR and stereo tools

engines.name: Edit page
engines.does: Timeline editor with trim tools, multicam, retime, titles, transitions and an effects library.

engines.name: Cut page
engines.does: Fast-assembly editing layout with Source Tape, dual timelines and smart edit commands.

engines.name: Fusion page
engines.does: Node-based compositor for 2D and 3D effects, motion graphics, tracking, keying, rotoscoping and particles.

engines.name: Color page
engines.does: Grading engine with primary and secondary tools, node graph, windows, tracking, scopes, HDR and colour management.

engines.name: Fairlight page
engines.does: Audio post engine: mixer, busses, ADR, foley, effects, loudness metering and automation.

engines.name: Deliver page
engines.does: Render queue and export settings for one or many jobs.

engines.name: Photo page (version 21)
engines.does: Applies the Color page toolset and node editor to still images including RAW.

engines.name: DaVinci Neural Engine
engines.does: Machine-learning features such as face recognition, region tracking and Magic Mask; Studio only.

capabilities.does: One smart trim tool switches among ripple, roll, slip and slide by pointer position. Also gives dynamic trimming during JKL playback, asymmetric trims in two directions, and trims across several clips and tracks.
capabilities.inputs: clips and edit points on the timeline
capabilities.outputs: changed clip boundaries and timeline length

capabilities.does: Dropping a clip on the timeline or timeline viewer shows an overlay of seven edit types: overwrite, insert (pushes later clips along), place on top, append at end, replace, fit to fill and ripple overwrite. Swap and shuffle commands rearrange clips already placed.
capabilities.inputs: source clips, in and out points, target tracks

capabilities.does: Several timelines can be open at once, stacked or in tabs, so material moves between them without leaving the page.

Plays 4, 9, 16, 25 or more angles together. Angles sync by audio waveform, timecode or in/out points. Switching is by keyboard or mouse, with video-only or audio-only cuts, and cuts can be refined later in the timeline.
capabilities.outputs: multicam clip with a cut between angles

capabilities.does: Retime a clip for slow or fast motion, with a graphical curve editor for frame position and speed. Fit to Fill adds an automatic speed change so a clip meets a chosen duration.
Retime quality can be optical flow, frame blending or nearest frame. A Studio-only advanced speed warp exists. The smooth cut transition uses optical flow to hide jump cuts.
An adjustment clip applies an effect or colour correction to all clips on the tracks below it.
A timeline curve editor shows keyframes and bezier ease curves under each clip for editing clip parameter animation.
Colour-coded markers carry titles, notes and keywords. On-screen annotations can be shared with remote collaborators.
Subtitles sit in a track above the video and can be moved and trimmed. Import accepts TTML, SRT, XML and subtitles embedded in MXF or IMF; export writes TTML, SRT and VTT.
capabilities.outputs: subtitle track or exported subtitle file

capabilities.does: Clips can be transcribed to produce subtitles or to drive text-based editing; the page gives no further detail.
Over 100 transitions including wipes and dissolves, plus over 80 CPU and GPU effects such as blurs, flares and warps. Third-party OpenFX plug-ins are also supported.
Image stabilisation with controls for camera lock, zoom, crop ratio, smoothing and strength.
Basic text generators for titles and lower thirds, a subtitle generator, and more than 100 Fusion-based title tools for animated 2D and 3D titles, with font and size controls in the inspector.
The media pool offers bins, smart bins and icon or list views for organising clips.
Several editors work in one project with bin and timeline locking and built-in chat.
Studio feature: an AI tool analyses a clip for people and creates a bin per person found.
Source Tape shows every clip in the current bin as one continuous tape in the viewer, so shots can be scrubbed and chosen visually.
The upper timeline shows the whole programme and the lower one a zoomed-in area for trimming.

Cut page commands: Smart Insert at the nearest edit point, Append at End, Place On Top, Ripple Overwrite and Source Overwrite. A smart indicator marks where an edit will land, so in and out points are often unnecessary.
The Sync Bin finds every clip synced to the timeline position and shows them in a multiview for choosing cutaways. It also serves multicam editing, not in real time.
Close Up uses the DaVinci Neural Engine to find faces in a shot and zoom in on them.
Compositing as a node flow. The effects library holds over 200 tools and a search window opens with Shift+Spacebar. Merge has background and foreground inputs; tools such as Blur take a mask input.

A 3D workspace with unlimited objects, lights and cameras joined by a 3D merge tool. Has image planes, spheres, text, FBX and Alembic import, shadow-casting spot lights, projection tools, set extensions and a 3D camera tracker.
Particle emitter and renderer nodes plus more than a dozen particle nodes. Forces model gravity, friction, turbulence and bounce, and the system works in 3D.
A planar tracker follows a flat surface so another image can be match-moved onto it.
A 2D tracker in match-move mode follows points; tracking data can animate masks. A Track forward button runs the analysis.
A 3D camera tracker is part of the Fusion toolset.
Delta Keyer with pre-matte, matte, fringe and tuning tabs, an eyedropper to sample the key colour, and a clean plate node.
Bezier and B-spline masks with per-point feathering, animatable and trackable by planar or 2D trackers.
Spline Editor with linear, Bezier and B-spline curves, reverse, loop and ping-pong strip, squish and stretch of keyframes, and copy-paste of curve shapes. A separate keyframe editor exists.
Parameters accept modifiers, including the follower modifier, and expressions.
The create-macro command turns a node group into a reusable tool that serves as an Edit-page template. Node versioning lets a user keep alternatives of one node setup.
Deep pixel compositing with EXR files that carry XYZ data; volumetric effects are GPU accelerated.

Fusion's Paint node has Stroke and Polyline Stroke brushes; an Apply Mode button switches from colour to a clone brush. Alt- or Option-click sets the clone source offset, which follows the stroke. The guide removes tracking markers on a frozen frame (pp. 93-96).

Keyframing a Transform node's position creates a path. Connecting the angle parameter to the path's Heading auto-orients an object along it. A path can also be painted with the Paint node's Polyline Stroke, which adds control points like a Bezier drawing tool (guide pp. 171-179).

Motion Blur is a checkbox on a Fusion node's Settings tab. Quality sets how many times the image is replicated; Shutter Angle mimics a camera shutter (360 is a full frame). Higher values raise render time (guide pp. 189-190).

The Fusion page sizes a composition from the original clip, not the timeline, so compositing runs at source resolution. On the Edit page, MediaOut scales the result to timeline resolution (guide p. 171). Two lessons cover retaining a clip's resolution and controlling a composition's.
Text+ makes 2D text and Text 3D makes 3D text. The follower modifier is listed among the animation modifiers.
Fusion has built-in Python and Lua scripting.
The Edit page lists a remote scripting API among the Studio-only items.
Version 21 release page names audio-driven Fusion animation as a new feature; no detail beyond the name was read.
Version 21 release page names an upgraded USD toolset in Fusion; no detail beyond the name was read.
Version 21 release page lists HTML graphics and Lottie support among new Edit-page features; no detail beyond the name was read.

Primary wheels for lift, gamma and gain with an offset wheel; controls for contrast, saturation, hue, temperature, tint, midtone detail and colour boost; primary bars; log wheels with tighter ranges; an auto colour button.
Custom curves for red, green, blue and luminance; five curves mapping one property to another (hue vs hue, hue vs sat, hue vs lum, lum vs sat, sat vs sat); a Colour Warper for hue targeting.
Qualifier palette selects areas by hue, saturation and luminance using an eyedropper and a key view.
Circle, curve, gradient and pen-drawn windows with size, softness, pan and rotation controls.
The tracker animates windows to follow objects, analysing pan, tilt, zoom, rotation and 3D perspective. It can also stabilise or attach effects.
A node editor builds corrections in sequence; Studio adds shared nodes that apply across several clips.
Built-in parade, waveform monitor, vectorscope, histogram and CIE chromaticity scopes.
Studio feature: HDR wheels and a zone-based HDR palette, Dolby Vision, HDR10+ and HDR Vivid metadata palettes, and ST.2084 or HLG tone mapping in colour space transforms.
Colour management with DaVinci colour management or ACES, using input, timeline and output transforms, tone mapping and LUT application.
Studio feature: temporal and spatial noise reduction in the motion effects palette, each applicable to chroma and luma noise.
An auto colour button and a Shot Match to This Clip command balance and match shots.
A RAW palette edits native camera RAW images directly.
Studio features: object removal and a Patch Replacer for removing unwanted elements.
Magic Mask is listed among Studio features and automatic AI region tracking by the Neural Engine; the pages give no parameters.

Over 90 Resolve FX plug-ins on the Color page, among them light effects (light rays, lens flare, aperture diffraction, lens reflection), Revival restoration, and Studio face refinement and Ultra Beauty.
Version 21 Photo page applies Resolve colour tools, a node editor, cropping, albums, search and AI tools to still images; the whats-new list gives names only.
With the Fairlight Audio Core, up to 2,000 tracks play with real-time effects. FlexBus busses reach 36 channels, each track sends to 20 bus sets of three, and adaptive tracks map up to 36 channels.
Busses for 5.1, 7.1 and 22.2 mastering. Studio adds immersive formats ASAF, Dolby Atmos and Audio Vivid with a 3D panner.

ADR sets up recording cues (beeps, countdowns, text prompts, streamers), keeps cue lists with character and dialogue, records multiple rated takes, and auditions sound effect libraries. A foley sampler plug-in is Studio only.
Over 25 Fairlight FX including noise reduction with a learn function; each clip and track has a 6-band EQ, expander or gate, compressor and limiter. Steinberg VST and Audio Unit plug-ins are hosted.
Monitoring panel with selectable metering standard and colour-coded meet, tolerance and exceed states, a live loudness graph for the main bus, and offline audio level analysis per clip.
Records control and effect changes over time, edited graphically per track, with a preview mode and latch touch control. Main and bus tracks can be automated too.
A render queue exports several jobs; Deliver page gives control over encoding options and formats.
Quick export uploads straight to YouTube, Vimeo and X; render options, remote rendering and workflow plug-ins appear as feature tiles, with no codec list on the page.
